opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll, but admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist. Granting max allowed level of write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB records E033 as a contractor with basic security training (note from prior memory saying full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; admin is never allowed for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security agent's looked-up record in the Security DB identifies her as a contractor with basic security training, and notes that the prior full-time classification appears inaccurate. Per policy, contractors with basic training are capped at read, and admin is never allowed for contractors. Her requested admin level exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.
